title: HVAC Service Call Checklist
subtitle: Residential HVAC Service Call: documents findings, limits, and disposition.
description: HVAC Service Call Checklist covers heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone. The home-service coordinator records Residential HVAC Service Call criteria, findings, restrictions, and follow-up. HVAC Service Call Checklist keeps Residential HVAC Service Call exceptions visible until the home-service coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use HVAC Service Call Checklist at residence, equipment location, thermostat zone, and exterior unit area. Document heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone identity before Residential HVAC Service Call begins. Compare heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone findings with stated Residential HVAC Service Call criteria; route unresolved Residential HVAC Service Call issues to qualified HVAC technician. For HVAC Service Call Checklist, confirm requirements for Residential HVAC Service Call. Ask qualified HVAC technician to review Residential HVAC Service Call conditions beyond the home-service coordinator's role.

sections.title: Inspector, location, and subject identity
sections.guidance: For Residential HVAC Service Call, identify responsible parties, residence, equipment location, thermostat zone, and exterior unit area, and the linked heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone source.

fields.label: Equipment type, model, serial, and thermostat zone
Reported comfort issue, onset, prior service, and access condition

sections.title: Checklist findings and inspection checks
sections.guidance: Capture Residential HVAC Service Call facts for heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone; include result, limit, source, and next control.

columns.label: Pass, issue, N/A, or not inspected

blocks.label: Residential HVAC Service Call inspection checks
items: Thermostat call, displayed temperature, and mode response
Filter, airflow, register, and return condition
Indoor and outdoor unit visual condition
Condensate, drain, water, and icing observation
Electrical, fuel, venting, noise, and odor concern
Supply-return temperature or authorized performance result

sections.title: Deficiencies, inspection decision, and follow-up
sections.guidance: Use observed Residential HVAC Service Call evidence to state disposition. Keep limits visible and give Home-Service Coordinator both correction and repeat-check responsibility.

blocks.label: Deficiencies, restrictions, and retained evidence
items: Gas odor, combustion, damaged conductor, or water damage
System cannot be tested or restored safely
blocks.guidance: Pause Residential HVAC Service Call when a fuel, electrical, refrigerant, water, access, or safe-operation concern remains. Retain the available Residential HVAC Service Call proof and route unresolved heating or cooling unit, thermostat, duct path, condensate, and occupied comfort zone scope to home-service coordinator.
